title: Articles
summary: a, an, the — and the many places where English uses none at all.
whyThisTopic: Bangla has no articles at all, so there is nothing to carry over — every a, an and the has to be learned from scratch. They also appear in almost every sentence you will ever say.

options.text: Can you give me many bread?

feedback.en: **many** counts separate things. Uncountable nouns take **much**.
feedback.bn: **many** আলাদা আলাদা জিনিস গোনে। Uncountable noun-এর সাথে **much** বসে।

options.text: Can you give me some bread?

feedback.en: Correct. This noun can't be counted, so **some** works where **a / an** can't.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। এই noun গণনা করা যায় না, তাই **a / an**-এর জায়গায় **some** বসে।

options.text: Can you give me a bread?

feedback.en: **a / an** means *one*, and this noun can't be counted one by one. Use **some**, or nothing at all.
feedback.bn: **a / an** মানে *একটি*, কিন্তু এই noun একটি-দুটি করে গোনা যায় না। **some** বসবে, নয়তো কিছুই নয়।

options.text: Can you give me two breads?
